The operator was removing a misfed sheet from the laminating press during a size changeover. The task was part of a changeover between jobs or products. Stage of the task: teardown or changeover. Method in effect: SW-508 Laminator Changeover. The task was not being performed as written. The difference from the written method was as follows: the written method requires the platens to cool below 120 degrees Fahrenheit before the press is entered, but the sheet was cleared at running temperature to save about forty minutes of cooling. Equipment involved: Laminating press LP-03, upper heated platen. Equipment state at the time: hot, de-energized and guard or cover removed. Equipment condition: normal working order, nothing outstanding. The object handled weighed under 10 lb. Handling difficulty: long - bar, pipe or sheet and shifting or flexible contents. It was held one hand and wearing gloves that affected the grip. PPE in use: safety glasses and general purpose gloves. This differed from the PPE specified for the task. The event was not witnessed and was self reported at the time. Immediately before the event: standing at the front of the press with the guard swung open and the right arm extended into the press about 18 inches, hand on the near corner of the sheet. Body position at the moment: reaching forward. At the moment of the event: the sheet tore as it was pulled, the right hand travelled forward, and the back of the hand contacted the underside of the upper heated platen. Immediately after the event: the hand was withdrawn immediately, the operator stepped back from the press and walked to the sink, and the changeover was stopped. The operator contacted a temperature extreme. Source: The upper heated platen of laminating press LP-03. Magnitude: About 300 degrees Fahrenheit at the platen surface. Contact lasted momentary - under a second. Isolation state: the source had not been allowed to cool. Point of contact: back of the right hand between the knuckles and the wrist. Force applied from above. Difference from a normal run of this task: The changeover was done between shifts rather than at the scheduled slot, so no time was allowed for the platens to cool. Conditions at the point of injury: hot and time or production pressure. Detail: The area in front of the press runs warm during a changeover and the crew were working to hand over at shift change. The event occurred in the last hour of the shift. No overtime was being worked. It happened within roughly half an hour in. The operator had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: Heat resistant gloves are specified in the risk assessment for this press but are not stocked at the station. A guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Detail: The front guard was swung open to reach the sheet, and opening it does not prevent access to the platens while they are hot. Stop-work opportunity: The changeover could have been left for the incoming shift once the platens had cooled, but the handover was already late. At the scene, the area was cooled under running water and a sterile dressing was applied. Detail: Held under cool running water for about 20 minutes. This was self-administered. Notified: the team lead and EHS. This happened within a few minutes. Afterwards, the equipment was stopped. Work at the location stopped. The operator was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
